in the best of the land make thy father and thy brethren to dwell; let them dwell in the land of Goshen; and if thou knowest any men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.”
And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said unto Jacob, “How old art thou?”

And Jacob said unto Pharaoh, “The days of the years of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty years; few and evil have the days of the years of my life been, and have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their pilgrimage.”
And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from before Pharaoh.
And Joseph provided for his father and his brothers; and as Pharaoh had commanded, he gave them a possession in the best of the land of Egypt, in the land of Rameses.
And Joseph would give to his father and to his brothers, and to all his father's household, to each man a portion of food, as he provided for them.

sections.title: In Egypt, the famine was severe, and the governance of Joseph was established.

verses.text: And there was no food in all the land; for the famine was very grievous; and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan were devastated by the famine.
And Joseph gathered all the silver that was found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan for the corn which they bought; and Joseph brought the silver into Pharaoh's house.

And the silver was lacking in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan; and all the Egyptians came unto Joseph, saying, "Give us bread; for why should we die in thy presence? For the silver is gone."
And Joseph said, "Bring your cattle; and I will give you for your cattle, if money fail."

And they brought their cattle unto Joseph; and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the asses; and he fed them with bread for all their cattle that year.

And that year was ended; and in the second year they came unto him and said, "We will not hide it from our lord, how that our money is spent; my lord also hath our herds of cattle; there is not ought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies and our lands."

Wherefore shall we die before thine eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants unto Pharaoh; and give us seed, that we may live, and not die, that the land be not desolate."
And Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh; for the Egyptians sold every man his field, because the famine prevailed over them; and the land became Pharaoh's.
And as for the people, he removed them to cities from one end of the borders of Egypt even to the other end thereof.
And Joseph bought not the land of the priests; for the priests had a portion assigned them of Pharaoh, and did eat their portion which Pharaoh gave them; wherefore they sold not their lands.
And Joseph said unto all the people of Egypt, “Behold, this day I have made you and your land servants unto Pharaoh; take ye seed for your sowing and the land shall be yours.
In the time of famine, let one fifth of the produce be given unto Pharaoh, and the four parts shall be for you, for your seed and for your food, and for all the households of your kindred.
And they said, “Thou hast saved us; we have found grace in the sight of our lord; and we will be servants unto Pharaoh.”
And Joseph made it a law in the land of Egypt, that apart from the priests' land, one fifth should be for Pharaoh, which law endureth unto this day.

sections.title: And Jacob sent word to Joseph, that he might receive him in his land.

verses.text: And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen; and she became a possession unto them; and they multiplied exceedingly.
And Jacob dwelt in the land of Egypt seventeen years; and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred forty and seven years.

And the day of the death of Israel drew near; and he called his son Joseph and said unto him, “If now I have found grace in thy sight, put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh, and deal kindly and truly with me; bury me not, I pray thee, in Egypt.
But I will lie with my fathers, and thou shalt carry me out of Egypt, and bury me in their burying place.” And he said, “I will do as thou hast said.” And he said, “Swear unto me.”
And Joseph said unto him, “I will do as thou hast said.” And Israel bowed himself upon the bed's head.

sections.title: And Jacob blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.

verses.text: And after this matter, it came to pass; “Behold, our father is ill,” they said to Joseph; and he took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and went.
And to Jacob, they said, “Behold, your son Joseph has come to you”; and Israel was revived, and he sat up on his bed.
Jacob said to Joseph, “God appeared to me in the land of Canaan at Luz and blessed me.”

And I said to you: “Behold, I have made you fruitful; I have multiplied you; and I will make you a multitude of people; and this land shall be yours, and after you, an everlasting inheritance for your descendants.”
Now, as for me, when I came from Paddan, your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt, shall be mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be as Reuben and Simeon to me.
And the children whom you beget after them shall be yours; they shall be called by the name of their brothers in their inheritance.
And when I came from Mesopotamia, and there was but a little way to go to Ephrath, Rachel died in the land of Canaan; and I buried her there on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.”
And Israel, seeing Joseph's sons, said, “Who are these?”
And Joseph said to his father, “These are my sons, whom God has given me in this place.” And Jacob said, “Bring them to me, I pray you, that I may bless them.”
And the eyes of Israel were dim with age, so that he could not see; and he brought them near to him; and he kissed them and embraced them.
And Israel said unto Joseph, "I am not separated from thee; behold, God hath also shown me thy seed."
And Joseph made haste to remove his garments; and he went down to the ground before him.
And Joseph took both of his sons, and he set Ephraim on his right hand toward Israel's left, and Manasseh on his left hand toward Israel's right; and he brought them near unto his father.
And Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it upon the head of Ephraim, who was the younger; and his left hand upon the head of Manasseh, guiding his hands wittingly.
And Jacob blessed them, and said, "The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day,

The Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth."
And Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, and it displeased him; and he held up his father's hand, to remove it from Ephraim's head unto Manasseh's head.
And Joseph said unto his father, "Not so, my father; for this is the firstborn; put thy right hand upon his head."

And his father refused, and said, "I know it, my son, I know it; he also shall become a people, and he also shall be great; but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations."
And he blessed them that day, saying, "In thee shall Israel bless, saying, God make thee as Ephraim and as Manasseh." And he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
And Israel said unto Joseph, “Behold, I die; and God shall be with you, and shall bring you again unto the land of your fathers;
And I will give thee the best of the spoil which I took from the Amorites with my sword and with my bow,” he said.

sections.title: And Jacob gathered his sons as he called them.

verses.text: And Jacob called his sons and said unto them, "Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you what shall befall you in the last days."
"Come, ye sons of Jacob, gather yourselves together; and hearken; your father Israel shall speak unto you."

"Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength; the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power: unstable as water, thou shalt not excel; because thou wentest up to thy father's bed; then defiledst thou it: he went up to my couch."
"For thou art as unstable as water; thou shalt not excel; because thou wentest up to thy father's bed; then defiledst thou it: he went up to my couch."
"Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations."
"O my soul, come not thou into their secret; unto their assembly, mine honor, be not thou united: for in their anger they slew a man, and in their self-will they digged down a wall."
"Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel."
"Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee."
"Judah is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?"
"The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be."
The horse shall be adorned with wine; and the horse's bridle shall be adorned with wine; he shall put on his garment with wine; and his covering shall be with the blood of the grape.
His eyes shall be more joyous than wine; and his teeth shall be whiter than milk.
"Zebulun shall dwell at the shore of the sea; he shall be as a haven for ships; and his border shall extend unto Sidon."
"Issachar is a strong donkey, crouching between two burdens; and he saw that rest was good, and the land was pleasant; and he bowed his shoulder to bear, and became a servant unto tribute."
And the rest shall be good, and the land shall be fruitful; in the time of harvest, the earth shall yield its increase, and he shall be a laborer.
"Dan shall judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel."
Dan shall be a serpent by the way, an adder in the path; that biteth the horse's heels, so that his rider shall fall backward.
And the Lord shall deliver him; He shall keep him.
"Gad, a troop shall overcome him; but he shall overcome at the last."
"Asher's bread shall be fat, and he shall yield royal dainties."
"Niftalem is a wide vine that gives beauty upon its fruit."
"Joseph is a beloved son; he is exceedingly dear to me, one who comforts and nurtures me; he is a beloved one who returns to me."
"By their counsel, they became lords; and the oppressors were their companions."
"But indeed, their oppressors were mightily oppressed; their hands were under the strong hand of Jacob; and there, before your father’s God, they prevailed against Israel."
"My God, help me; bless me from above in the heavens, in all that is found therein; bless me on the earth, bless me in the womb and in the birth, bless me as You have blessed."

"The blessings of your father and your mother are stronger than the blessings of the mountains; they are mightier than the blessings of the everlasting hills; they shall rest upon Joseph’s head; they shall be upon the head of him who is the leader among his brothers."
"Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours the prey, and in the evening he divides the spoil for the people."
"These are all the twelve sons of Jacob; their father spoke this concerning them; he blessed them; and he blessed each one as he had blessed them."

sections.title: The Death and Burial of Jacob

verses.text: እንዲህም ብሎ አዘዛቸው፥ “እኔ ወደ ወገኖች እሰበሰባለሁ፤ በኬጢያዊው በኤፍሮን እርሻ ላይ ባለችው ዋሻ ከአባቶች ጋር ቅበሩኝ፤ እርስዋም በከነዓን ምድር በመምሬ ፊት ያለች፥
አብርሃም ለመቃብር ርስት ከኬጢያዊው ከኤፍሮን ከእርሻው ጋር የገዛት፥ ባለ ድርብ ክፍል ዋሻ ናት።
አብርሃምንና ሚስቱ ሣራንም በዚያ ቀበሩአቸው፤ ይስሐቅንና ሚስቱ ርብቃንም በዚያ ቀበሩአቸው፤ ከዚያም እኔ ልያን ቀበርኋት
እርሻውና በእርስዋ ላይ ያለችው ዋሻ ከኬጢ ልጆች የተገዙ ናቸው።”
ያዕቆብም ትእዛዙን ለልጆቹ ተናግሮ በፈጸመ ጊዜ እግሮቹን በአልጋው ላይ ዘርግቶ ሞተ፤ ወደ ወገኖቹም ተጨመረ።
ዮሴፍም በአባቱ ፊት ወደቀ፤ በእርሱም ላይ አለቀሰ፤ ሳመውም።
ዮሴፍም ባለ መድኀኒቶች አገልጋዮቹ አባቱን በሽቱ ያሹት ዘንድ አዘዘ፤ ባለ መድኀኒቶችም እስራኤልን በሽቱ አሹት።
አርባ ቀንም ፈጸሙለት፤ ሽቱ የሚቀቡበትን ቀን እንዲሁ ይቈጥራሉና፤ የግብፅም ሰዎች ሰባ ቀን አለቀሱለት።
የልቅሶውም ወራት ከተፈጸመ በኋላ ዮሴፍ ለፈርዖን መኳንንት እንዲህ ብሎ ተናገረ፥ “እኔ በፊታችሁ ሞገስን አግኝቼ እንደ ሆንሁ ለፈርዖን እንዲህ ብላችሁ ስለ እኔ ንገሩት፦
አባቴ ሳይሞት አምሎኛል፤ እንዲህ ሲል፦ ‘እነሆ እኔ እሞታለሁ፤ በቈፈርሁት መቃብር በከነዓን ምድር በዚያ ቅበረኝ።’ አሁንም ወጥቼ አባቴን ልቅበርና ልመለስ።”
ፈርዖንም ዮሴፍን አለው፥ “ውጣ፤ አባትህንም እንዳማለህ ቅበረው።”
ዮሴፍም አባቱን ሊቀብር ወጣ፤ የፈርዖን ሎሌዎችም ሁሉ፥ የቤቱ ሽማግሌዎችም ሁሉ፥ የግብፅ ምድር ሽማግሌዎችም ሁሉ ከእርሱ ጋር ወጡ፤
የዮሴፍም ቤተ ሰቦች ሁሉ፥ ወንድሞቹም፥ የአባቱም ቤተ ሰቦች ወጡ፤ ልጆቻቸውንና በጎቻቸውን፥ ከብቶቻቸውንም ብቻ በጌሤም ተዉ።
ሰረገሎችም፥ ፈረሰኞችም ከእርሱ ጋር ወጡ፤ ሠራዊቱም ብዙ ነበር።
በዮርዳኖስ ማዶ ወዳለችው ወደ አጣድ አውድማ ደረሱ፤ እጅግ ታላቅ በሆነ በጽኑ ልቅሶም አለቀሱለት፤ ለአባቱም ሰባት ቀን ልቅሶ አደረገለት።

And the inhabitants of that land, the Canaanites, said in those days, "Is the mourning of Egypt thus great?" Therefore, they called that place "Abel Mizraim," and he was buried in the valley of Jordan.
And his sons did unto him as he had commanded them.

And his sons returned to the land of Canaan; and they buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which is before Mamre, the field which Abraham purchased from Ephron the Hittite for a possession of a burying place.
And Joseph and his brethren, and all the company that went up with him to bury his father, returned into the land of Egypt after he had buried his father.

sections.title: Joseph and his brethren were reconciled.

verses.text: የዮሴፍም ወንድሞች አባታቸው እንደ ሞተ በአዩ ጊዜ እንዲህ አሉ፥ “ምናልባት ዮሴፍ ያደረግንበትን ክፋት ያስብብን ይሆናል፤ ባደረግንበትም ክፋት ሁሉ ብድራት ይመልስብን ይሆናል።”
ወደ ዮሴፍም መጡ፤ እንዲህም አሉት፥ “አባትህ ገና ሳይሞት እንዲህ ብሎ አዝዟል፦
‘ዮሴፍን እንዲህ በሉት፦ እባክህ የወንድሞችህን በደል ኀጢአታቸውንም ይቅር በል፤ እነርሱ በአንተ ክፉ አድርገውብሃልና፤’ አሁንም እባክህ የአባትህ አምላክ ባሪያዎች የበደሉህን ይቅር በል።”
ዮሴፍም ይህን ሲሉት አለቀሰ። ወንድሞቹ ደግሞ መጡ፤ “እነሆ፥ እኛ ለአንተ አገልጋዮችህ ነን” አሉት።
ዮሴፍም አላቸው፥ “አትፍሩ፤ ይህ ከእግዚአብሔር ዘንድ ሆኖአልና።
እናንተ በእኔ ላይ ክፉ መከራችሁ፤ እግዚአብሔር ግን ዛሬ እንደ ሆነው ብዙ ሕዝብ እንዲመገብ ለማድረግ ለእኔ መልካም መከረ።
አሁንም አትፍሩ፤ እኔ እናንተንና ቤተ ሰቦቻችሁን እመግባችኋለሁ።” አጽናናቸውም፤ በልባቸው የሚገባ ነገርም ነገራቸው።

sections.title: The Death of Joseph

verses.text: And Joseph dwelt in the land of Egypt; he and his brethren, and the house of his father; and Joseph was seventeen years old.
And Joseph saw the children of Ephraim unto the third generation; the children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were brought up upon Joseph's knees.
And Joseph said unto his brethren, “I die; and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which He swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”
And Joseph spake unto the children of Israel, saying, “God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.”
And Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old; and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
